# Alt Text Checker

> Free, browser-only alt text checker. A bookmarklet audits every image on the page you are viewing (missing alt, empty alt, file-name or generic alt, "image of" prefixes, alt over 125 characters, duplicate alt, image-only links with no text, unnamed SVGs, CSS background images) and exports a CSV. You can also paste a page's HTML, or fetch a URL when the site allows cross-origin requests. Includes an alt text writing guide with good and bad examples, a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 reference, and a step-by-step alt text helper. No sign-up, no tracking, nothing leaves the browser.

URL: https://lab.zalastack.com/alt-text-checker/

## Key facts

- WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): non-text content needs a text alternative that serves the same purpose; decorative images must be hidden from assistive technology (for images, alt="").
- alt="" is correct for decorative images. A missing alt attribute is an error; screen readers may read the file name instead.
- An image that is the only content of a link or button needs alt text describing the destination or action (WCAG 1.1.1, 2.4.4, 4.1.2).
- WCAG sets no length limit for alt text. About 125 characters is a common rule of thumb; longer descriptions belong in a caption or nearby text.
- CSS background images cannot have alt text; meaningful content in them should be real text or an img element.
- Related criteria: 1.4.5 Images of Text (AA), 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception) (AAA), 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A), 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A).

| Image type | Good alt |
|---|---|
| Informative photo | What it shows that matters in this context |
| Decorative | alt="" |
| Link or button | The action or destination, e.g. "Search" |
| Logo | The organization name; "Name home" if it links home |
| Text in image | The exact words |
| Chart | Type plus takeaway, with full data in nearby text or a table |
